title: BA (Hons) Business Management
description: Picture the role, the salary and the life. A flexible degree built for working adults — funding and outcomes mapped before you apply.

section_3.title: A practical degree, built around your life.
section_3.description: A career-focused undergraduate degree for students who want a professionally relevant qualification they can study alongside work or family.

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.description: Working adults already in business roles, career changers moving into management, and mature students returning to education who need a structured but flexible pathway. Many students are in their 30s and 40s, balancing work, family and study.

cards.title: What you'll learn
cards.description: Core business disciplines — management, marketing, operations, finance, strategy and leadership — plus transferable skills employers value: data analysis, professional communication, project planning and critical thinking.

cards.title: Assessment style
cards.description: A mix of coursework, group projects and presentations, with fewer traditional written exams than most people expect. This often suits mature students who prefer applied learning over exam technique.

section_15.title: Questions before applying.
section_15.description: Clear answers reduce uncertainty before you apply.

faqs.question: Can I get Maintenance Loan for this course?
faqs.answer: Potentially, if the course and study mode meet the rules and you are personally eligible. Always check before applying.

faqs.question: Can I study while working?
faqs.answer: This route is positioned for working adults, but you should check the exact attendance pattern before applying.

faqs.question: Do I need A Levels?
faqs.answer: Not always. Mature students may have alternative qualifications, access courses or experience-based routes.

faqs.question: What jobs can this lead to?
faqs.answer: Common routes include business analyst, operations manager, project coordinator, team leader and commercial roles.

faqs.question: Can I transfer credits?
faqs.answer: If you have HNC, HND or previous university study, ask an adviser to check possible advanced entry routes.
